card.summary: Free users: 2 tunnels, 10 Mbps limit, traffic claimable by daily check-in; real-name verification raises the limit to 25 Mbps. [translated from a forum roundup]

free_tier.stated: Free users: 2 tunnels, 10 Mbps limit, traffic claimable by daily check-in; real-name verification raises the limit to 25 Mbps. [translated from a forum roundup]

egress.terms: Traffic is granted by daily check-in; no monthly byte allowance is published in available documentation.; ingress: udp

record.interface_detail: frpc client, Docker image, web panel.
record.chaining: Same shape as ChmlFrp: a UDP tunnel that can carry a WG datagram, capped at 10 Mbps free.
record.binding_note: The byte allowance is a check-in grant of unknown size, so the quota is what fails first and it cannot be shown to reach 1 TiB without measuring the grant.

identity_cost.detail: Account registration is by email; real-name verification is optional and buys a higher speed cap (25 Mbps instead of 10 Mbps) according to the roundup.

record.reliability_note: Free-tier throughput depends on a daily claim; a missed day is a metering event, not an outage.
record.confidence_note: The pricing table 404s and the panel is behind a login, so the numbers are the roundup author's. Reading the panel would raise it to documented.

evidence.proved: 2 tunnels, 10 Mbps, check-in traffic, 25 Mbps after real-name
the service is live and reports 74.33 TB of carried traffic

record.notes: mefrp.com/pricing returns a 404 today, so the free tier is only described by the forum roundup. The operator's home page claims 69 nodes and 74.33 TB carried, which is consistent with a real service.

extras.wg_detail: frp-family service; UDP tunnels are the transport for a WG datagram.
extras.volume_stated: Traffic is granted by daily check-in.
extras.transit_note: ME Frp nodes relay the datagrams.
